 October’s Tunnel Fits we can’t stop thinking about 
 From sharp custom suits to bold casual statements, here are the top 10 tunnel fits setting the tone for autumn style
 Vinciane Ngomsi 
 October 27, 2026 
 Topics: 
 Fashion 
 Tunnel Fits 
 Up Next From Culture

 With the NBA back, the NFL in full swing and the WNBA playoffs underway, narrowing October’s top looks down to 10 was a challenge. You’ll see several suits ahead, but some of these casual ensembles look easy to recreate and deserve a mention.
 While tailored sets remain a staple of the tunnel, other picks include more relaxed outfits that make a case for everyday style. Scroll on to see who made the cut, and consider the bar raised for November.
 Patrick Mahomes 
 Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes arrives at Allegiant Stadium on Oct. 4 for a game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Chris Unger/Getty Images
 Patrick Mahomes made a statement before kickoff, arriving at the Kansas City Chiefs’ NFL matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders in a burgundy and cream pinstripe suit. Designed by Stephen Richards Jr. of Richards Bespoke, the custom three-piece suit featured a patterned tie, dark horsebit loafers and Oakley shades, proving he still knows how to make an entrance.
 LeBron James 
 Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James arrives at Madison Square Garden before a game against the New York Knicks on Oct. 20. David L. Nemec/NBAE via Getty Images
 New team, same commitment to the drip. In his first regular-season game as a 76er, King James stepped out in a dark double-breasted suit, a crisp white shirt and sunglasses. Keeping things classic with a no-tie look and polished footwear, the 41-year-old showed that a team change doesn’t mean style takes a hit.

 CeeDee Lamb 
 View this post on Instagram 
 CeeDee Lamb may have taken a few notes from Beyoncé’s Cowboy Carter era. For the Dallas Cowboys’ home game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Oct. 8, the All-Pro receiver arrived in a custom Nike look, featuring a fringed brown-and-yellow jacket, a bolo tie, a cowboy hat, a statement belt buckle, and a bright red bag. 
 DeWanna Bonner 
 The Atlanta Dream’s DeWanna Bonner arrives before a game against the New York Liberty on Oct. 4 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. Adam Hagy/NBAE via Getty Images
 DeWanna Bonner put a fresh spin on office attire ahead of the Atlanta Dream’s playoff matchup against the New York Liberty. She paired a crisp white button-down and black tie with tailored shorts, sheer tights and pointed-toe heels, then added a black clutch and gold jewelry to finish a look that means business.

 Zaire Franklin 
 View this post on Instagram 
 Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin went monochromatic for his Week 6 look, and the burgundy leather ensured he stood out. He paired a matching leather jacket and pants with a black shirt, tinted sunglasses and patterned shoes, finishing the look with an oversized “Z” pendant.
 A’ja Wilson 
 Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson celebrates winning her fifth WNBA Most Valuable Player award on Oct. 8 in Las Vegas. David Becker/NBAE via Getty Images
 A’ja Wilson celebrated her record-breaking fifth WNBA Most Valuable Player award in a bold red, double-breasted Dolce & Gabbana suit. She finished the look with black-rimmed glasses — an outfit only the face of the league could pull off. 
 Kaila Charles 
 Kaila Charles of the Golden State Valkyries arrives in style before Game 3 of the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream on Oct. 21 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. Jonathan Bachman/NBAE via Getty Images
 Kaila Charles brought animal print to Game 3 of the WNBA Finals, pairing a red ruched leather top with oversized cheetah-print shorts and knee-high black boots — a statement look that proves WNBA players are trendsetters.

 Spike Lee 
 Filmmaker Spike Lee attends the reigning NBA champion New York Knicks’ ring ceremony at Madison Square Garden before a game against the Philadelphia 76ers on Oct. 20. Sarah Stier/Getty Images
 Spike Lee clearly had this one saved for a very special occasion. The longtime New York Knicks fan showed up for the team’s opening-night championship celebration at Madison Square Garden in an orange-and-blue pinstriped suit, complete with a matching hat, boots and Knicks backpack.
 Related Story

 Jared McCain 
 The Oklahoma City Thunder’s Jared McCain arrives to the arena before the game against the LA Clippers on Oct. 25 at Paycom Center. Zach Beeker/NBAE via Getty Images
 Jared McCain kept it neutral for his Oct. 25 pregame arrival, pairing a textured cream-colored Bode cardigan with relaxed white denim trousers from Our Legacy. Orange-tinted sunglasses, a Louis Vuitton monogram crossbody bag and brown square-toe boots add personality to the cream look while still keeping it cohesive.

 Jaylen Brown 
 The Philadelphia 76ers’ Jaylen Brown arrives before a game against the New York Knicks on Oct. 20 at Madison Square Garden in New York. Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images
 For NBA opening night, Jaylen Brown wore an oversized black leather jacket with red detailing over a black turtleneck and wide-leg trousers. Mirror-finish silver sneakers, small wraparound sunglasses and a slouchy black leather duffel completed the slightly futuristic look.
 Paul Pogba 
 French professional soccer player Paul Pogba walks onto the field before the New Orleans Saints-Pittsburgh Steelers NFL game at Stade de France on Oct. 25 in Paris. Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images
 Soccer star Paul Pogba arrived for the NFL’s first-ever Paris game over the weekend wearing a dark denim jacket with contrasting black sleeves, a black turtleneck and matching denim pants. A newsboy cap and round sunglasses completed the look. While there, the 2018 World Cup winner put his camera skills to work , capturing action between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints.
 Vinciane is a storyteller and digital content creator. When she's not covering all things women's sports, sneakers, soccer and tennis, catch her (still) learning the moves to every iconic Beyoncé dance break, stressing out about Manchester United or cooking.
